title: resident-set-drift-and-prefetch-adaptation-field-diary
content:
Context:
This is a working diary documenting a set of exploratory experiments to quantify 'resident-set drift' across hours-of-day and to prototype an adaptive prefetch controller that changes prefetch window and aggressiveness based on measured drift + bank saturation signals. Goal is to reduce unnecessary NVMe reads during drift events while avoiding tail-latency regressions for long-seqlen requests.

Motivation / observed problem:
- Recent tenant incidents show spikes in NVMe read IO even when aggregate reuse rate looks OK. Hypothesis: drift in which embeddings/kv pages are hot (resident-set drift) causes prefetch to incorrectly warm pages that are no longer in the active hotset, increasing read amplification and bandwidth.
- Static prefetch windows (N pages ahead) tuned for average workload amplify waste when working sets shift quickly (e.g., short marketing-burst traffic mixed with background large-seqlen batch).

Definitions used in experiments:
- resident-set drift metric (RSD): fraction of top-k hot pages at T that are not in top-k at T-Δ. Computed per shard and scaled to 0..1.
- reuse_rate: tokens served that hit KV cache / total tokens requiring KV accesses.
- prefetch_hit_fraction: fraction of prefetch reads that were subsequently used within 5s.
- bank_saturation: instantaneous memory channel utilization sampled at 100ms granularity (normalized 0..1).

Experiment 1: Drift timeseries and taxonomy
- Data: 72-hour trace sampled from production dev cluster (mixed tenant mix, seqlen mix: 70% short <128, 20% mid 128-1024, 10% long >1024).
- Method: compute RSD with k=4096 every 1 minute using sliding 5-minute windows. Correlate with NVMe read/s, reuse_rate, prefetch_hit_fraction.
- Findings: persistent low-drift baseline RSD ~0.12 during steady traffic. Short-lived bursts (5–20 min) push RSD to 0.45–0.6 and correlate with a 2.8x spike in NVMe read/s and a 30-40% drop in prefetch_hit_fraction. Reuse_rate dropped from 0.78 -> 0.52 during bursts.
- Interpretation: bursts introduce new hotkeys that invalidate previous prefetch, causing prefetch misses and increased SSD reads. Static prefetch causes wasted IO during those transitions.

Experiment 2: Bank-aware backpressure overlay
- Prototype: controller takes bank_saturation and RSD. If RSD > 0.35 AND bank_saturation > 0.6, throttle prefetch rate by halving inflight prefetches and increase prefetch delay by 50ms. Otherwise use baseline aggressive policy.
- Microbench: replay 30-minute burst traces with controller vs baseline.
- Result: controller reduced NVMe read/s peak by ~46%, prefetch_hit_fraction recovered to 0.68 (vs 0.55 baseline during bursts). End-to-end P99 tail latency for long seqlen requests improved by ~12% compared to baseline. CPU overhead negligible (<1% of worker cpu).
- Caveat: some cold-start token latency increased for first request after throttle (avg +14ms). Acceptable for our SLO? Discuss.

Experiment 3: Sliding-exponential drift estimator for prefetch window sizing
- Idea: adjust prefetch lookahead size (pages) per-shard with a multiplicative factor derived from exponential-weighted RSD (alpha=0.25). Larger recent RSD => shrink window.
- Config tested: base-window 32 pages; window multiplier m = clip(1 - 1.5*E[RSD], 0.4, 1.2).
- Result: adaptive-window reduced wasted prefetch reads by 37% while keeping reuse_rate within 3% of baseline in steady-state. During very fast drift (RSD > 0.6) adaptive policy outperforms baseline by cutting NVMe load and preventing SLO violations.

Experiment 4: Cohort-aware policy by seqlen mix
- Observation from traces: short-seq dominated tenants have more volatile RSD (higher churn), long-seq tenants have stable hotset.
- Policy: tag requests by seqlen cohort and maintain per-cohort prefetch aggressiveness and cache admission.
- Result: isolating cohorts reduced cross-tenant eviction pressure; mixed workloads saw reuse_rate for long-cohort increase from 0.82 -> 0.88, at expense of short-cohort reuse dropping 0.02 but with much lower NVMe spikes. Overall unit cost improved ~6%.

Telemetry & instrumentation notes (what we added)
- RSD counter per shard (1m agg) + drift-spike alarm when >0.35 sustained for >3m.
- Prefetch_hit_fraction histogram by tenant and shard (1m).
- Bank_saturation sampling integrated from the memory telemetry agent at 100ms resolution.

Controller pseudocode (simplified)
- every 250ms per-shard:
    rsd = ewma(rsd_sample, 0.25)
    bank = sample_bank_saturation()
    if rsd > 0.35 and bank > 0.6:
        prefetch.max_inflight = baseline_inflight / 2
        prefetch.delay_ms = baseline_delay * 1.5
    else if rsd > 0.2:
        prefetch.max_inflight = baseline_inflight * 0.75
    else:
        prefetch.restore_baseline()

Operational runbook snippets
- If drift alarm fires: temporarily enable bank-aware throttle; check tenant traffic spikes in the last 10m; if a single tenant caused the spike, consider isolating traffic via route-pin.
- If NVMe Q1 latency > 10ms concurrently with RSD > 0.4: escalate to infra and consider increasing swapback budget or enabling conservative admission for the offending shard.

Open questions / failure modes
- RSD sensitivity to k: we used k=4096; smaller k picks up micro-hotkeys faster but noisier. Need to run auto-tune sweep across different HW sizes.
- Multi-shard correlation: hotset migration across shards (due to hashing changes or re-sharding) might create false-positive drift. Need shard-mapping-aware RSD.
- Long-term: adversarial tenants might oscillate hotkeys to force cache churn. Consider fairness guardrails and per-tenant admission quotas.

Next steps / roadmap (short term)
- Stabilize telemetry and ship RSD + prefetch_hit_fraction to telemetry-prod. (Priya to own)
- Landing PR with bank-aware throttle + toggles behind feature flag (PR #1427 linked). (Diego owner)
- Run 1-week A/B with 10% traffic on canary cluster and measure cost, tail latency, NVMe read/s. Collect tenant-level delta. (Samir owner)

Notes to self / running log
- 2024-11-07: started trace extraction, initial RSD plots show clear diurnal pattern on US-west clusters.
- 2024-11-09: bank_saturation probe implemented; initial false positives due to sampling jitter — smoothed with 3-sample median.
- 2024-11-13: prototype controller reduced SSD spikes in replay. Need real-world canary.
- 2024-11-20: assembled runbook entries and added linked artifacts above. Preparing canary staging rollout.

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot (representative from replay)
- baseline reuse_rate: 0.78
- reuse_rate during burst (baseline): 0.52
- reuse_rate during burst (adaptive controller): 0.69
- peak NVMe read/s baseline: 4800 IO/s
- peak NVMe read/s adaptive: 2600 IO/s
- P99 token latency (long seqlen) baseline: 220ms
- P99 token latency adaptive: 194ms

If anyone wants raw traces or the notebook used for analysis, ping me and I will drop the query + minimal notebook into the PR workspace. This doc will be iterated — feedback welcome, especially on thresholds (rsd 0.35) and the bank_saturation breakpoint.
-- Avery
